title: Kiosk reservation battery checklist
lede: A reservation for ten batteries is now presented as one quantity to fulfill, while actual unit numbers remain visible only after the physical batteries are scanned.

stats.n: Ten misleading numbered placeholders become one quantity row
Actual scanned unit numbers remain recorded and visible

sections.heading: Reservation pickup
sections.note: Same reservation-battery fixture, same cart, same iPad Air 11-inch (M4), iOS 26.5 simulator viewport.

pairs.title: What the operator scans
pairs.sub: Read the right-hand checklist and the battery guidance above the action.
pairs.beforeCap: The source checklist expanded a quantity of ten into Battery 1 through Battery 10, which suggested those exact units were required.
pairs.afterCap: The checklist now says 10 × V-Mount Battery and ANY UNITS; the physical unit number is shown after a successful scan rather than treated as a required list number.

changes.was: Unscanned reservation slots were shown as #1, #2, and so on, even though the pickup scan service accepts any available unit from the reserved family.
changes.now: Numbered placeholders are grouped into one quantity row. The slot IDs still drive confirmation, while actual scanned unit tags remain visible for custody.

changes.h: Battery guidance now answers the likely question
changes.was: The list did not explain whether the printed number had to match.
changes.now: The Kiosk explicitly says to scan any available units and that printed unit numbers do not need to match the list.

verification: Focused native source-contract tests: 6/6 passing across reservation pickup, grouped battery presentation, and safe unit-chip rendering.
Native: WisconsinKiosk Debug and Release builds pass; project parity, drift, and iOS gap audits pass.
Visual: matched baseline/final captures inspected on the available iPad Air 11-inch (M4), iOS 26.5 simulator.
Docs: npm run verify:docs remains blocked by pre-existing generated codemap drift in architecture, backend, and areas; dirty codemaps were preserved.
notes: This changes presentation only. The pickup scan and confirmation APIs remain unchanged, and exact physical unit allocation/audit semantics remain authoritative.

The Kiosk target has no dedicated UI-test target in the current project; the repeatable DEBUG fixture was launched with simctl after native compilation. No live credentials or production data were used.
Physical managed-iPad/scanner acceptance and deployment remain open.
